title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Alternative Methods - Emergency Purchases
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A severe storm has destroyed the roof of the city's main water treatment plant, causing an immediate threat to the public water supply. The buyer should process the replacement as a(n):
options: Emergency Purchase
Single Source Procurement
Sole Source Procurement
Pilot Program
questions.explain: An emergency purchase is justified when there is an immediate threat to public health, welfare, or safety, or to prevent severe damage to government property.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A department forgot to submit a requisition for standard seasonal supplies, and they are now out of stock just as their busy season begins. The department requests an emergency purchase to avoid downtime. How should the buyer proceed?
options: Process as an emergency due to the operational downtime risk
Deny the emergency request because poor planning does not constitute a valid emergency
Process as a sole source to expedite delivery
Approve it as a single source exception
questions.explain: Failure to plan properly by a department does not legally constitute an emergency. Emergency exceptions are reserved for true, unforeseeable threats to health, safety, or property.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency is executing an emergency purchase to fix a collapsed sewer line. Which of the following limits should strictly apply to this emergency procurement?
options: The procurement should be limited to the materials and services necessary to alleviate the immediate threat
The procurement should include preventive maintenance for all other sewer lines in the city
The procurement requires an IFB to be published on a 5-day accelerated timeline
The contract awarded must be a firm-fixed-price 5-year agreement
questions.explain: Emergency procurements must be strictly limited in scope to what is absolutely necessary to resolve the immediate threat. Any subsequent, non-immediate work must be competitively bid.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If a situation arises outside of normal business hours that constitutes a true emergency, end-user departments are typically authorized to bypass formal competition, but they are still required to:
options: Wait until the procurement office opens to issue a PO
Issue an RFP within 24 hours of the emergency
Maintain thorough documentation justifying the emergency and keep costs as low as reasonably possible given the circumstances
Sole source the rest of the agency's needs for the year to the responding vendor
questions.explain: Emergency purchases allow bypassing the normal time-consuming bid process, but agencies must heavily document the nature of the emergency, why competition was bypassed, and efforts made to ensure fair pricing.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios absolutely does NOT meet the legal standard for an emergency purchase?
options: A generator failure at an active public hospital
A sudden bridge collapse on a major thoroughfare
A fiscal year-end deadline approaching, and the department wants to spend remaining funds before they expire
A breach in a public data server actively leaking citizen social security numbers
questions.explain: Expiring funds and failure to plan do not constitute an emergency. Emergencies are strictly physical, operational, or health/safety threats.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Following an emergency purchase, best practice and most public procurement statutes require the procurement officer to:
options: Place the vendor on a permanent do-not-call list
File a written determination outlining the basis of the emergency and the vendor selection for the procurement file
Demand the vendor discount their invoice by 15%
Immediately issue a new RFP for the exact same services
questions.explain: Accountability is paramount. Even when competition is bypassed due to a threat, a formal, written determination of the emergency must be added to the public file to justify the action.
